lessons.title: Classification, then assignment
lessons.why: Unified routing is two stages. Mixing them makes the wrong control look broken.
depends: Dynamics 365 Contact Center or Customer Service
body: The unified-routing overview applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center embedded, Contact Center standalone, and Customer Service. It says unified routing has two stages. In classification, rules and machine-learning models can add information on the work item. In assignment, requests are prioritized and then assigned using the nature of the work, related entities, skills, and the current availability and workload.

The page says you configure unified routing in the Copilot Service admin center, and that representatives must use the Copilot Service workspace app to be assigned work. It says unified routing is not supported in Unified Service Desk. Intelligent skill finder depends on an AI Builder category classification model, so AI Builder has to be available in the region where you use it. The page says unified routing is supported in the same regions as Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This room does not copy that region list.

lessons.say: Classification adds information. Assignment uses it. They are not the same stage.
lessons.fault: A skill is missing and the assignment method is rebuilt before anyone checks classification.
lessons.listen: Unified routing classifies a work item, then assigns it. Representatives use Copilot Service workspace. Unified Service Desk is not supported.

lessons.title: Voice workstreams and voice queues
lessons.why: A voice workstream will not offer pick mode. The page says push only, and the choice cannot be edited later.
body: The workstreams page says a workstream is a container to enrich, route, and assign work items. Types are Messaging, Record, and Voice. Voice routes calls to support numbers. In the create dialog, Push sends the work with a message alert, and Pick waits until someone takes it from Open work items. For voice, push mode only is available, and the work distribution mode cannot be edited later. A fallback queue receives work when no route-to-queue rule identifies a queue.

The assignment-methods page says least active is the default selection when you create a voice or messaging queue, and that it is for those channels only. The same page says the Queue priority field orders work across queues: work from higher-priority queues is assigned first. When queues mix out-of-the-box methods and custom prioritization, the page says the out-of-the-box queues are prioritized first. This room does not copy the assignment scale limits. The page links them.

lessons.title: Highest capacity, round robin, least active
lessons.why: The assignment method is a choice on the queue. The page defines three out-of-the-box methods this room can repeat.
body: Highest capacity assigns to the representative with the highest available capacity who has the skills from classification and an allowed presence. If more than one has the same capacity, the page says round-robin order breaks the tie. Exact match filters on an exact skill match and then orders by available capacity. Closest match orders by closest match rather than by available capacity. Advanced round robin matches skills, presence, and capacity. The initial order is when the user was added to the queue, then the order updates from assignments, and the order is kept per queue. A tie uses the earliest last-assignment time.

Least active, for voice and messaging only, uses the time since last capacity was released for a voice or messaging conversation and the Block capacity for wrap-up setting. The page says that data is in the msdyn_agentchannelstate table. First-in-first-out is the default prioritization when an out-of-the-box or custom method has no prioritization rules. For chat and voice, the page says the system uses conversation creation time. The page says not to use least active for employment decisions such as compensation, rewards, or seniority. Custom methods do not inherit the workstream’s presence, capacity, and skill settings. You configure those rules yourself.

chart.title: Three methods
chart.note: Names from one page. Not a productivity score.

lessons.say: I can name which assignment method the queue uses, and I will not use it to rank employees.
lessons.fault: Closest match is expected to order by free capacity, which is the exact-match behavior instead.
lessons.listen: Highest capacity uses free capacity. Round robin keeps an order per queue. Least active uses the last capacity release, and it is not for employment decisions.

lessons.title: Forecast, capacity, and schedule
lessons.why: Workforce management in this stack starts as a forecast of volume and handle time. It is not a Teams calling policy.
body: The forecasting overview says a forecast estimates volume and average handle time by channel and queue. Volume excludes conversations that AI agents handle with no representative joining. Forecasting is the first stage. Capacity planning uses the default forecast snapshot to calculate staffing requirements. Scheduling turns those requirements into shifts.

A short-term scenario is 15-minute intervals for a horizon of up to six weeks, which the page also states as 42 days, using a linear trend on internal or external data. A long-term scenario is daily, for up to three years, stated as 1,096 days. Weighted average is marked preview, uses external data, and refreshes manually. The page says not to use the feature for employment decisions. It also says forecasts might not account for unexpected trends. This room does not copy a shrinkage percentage. The Erlang calculator elsewhere in this campus stays a teaching model.

lessons.title: Indicators and guardrails
lessons.why: A quality indicator produces a score. A guardrail produces a violation. The page treats them as different objects.
body: The quality and coaching page applies to Dynamics 365 Contact Center only. An evaluation plan sets the criteria, which conversations, the timing, and the actions. Frequency is In real time, during the conversation, or On conversation close, after it ends. Conditions pick the queue or workstream. Sampling is a percentage. Real-time actions can notify a supervisor, send a coaching nudge, or both, for ranges the page names Critical, Warning, and Normal. On conversation close, weights say how much each indicator contributes.

Indicators are questions with scores. Answer types on the page include Yes/No, multi-select, and single select. Guardrails are required or prohibited behaviors. They are evaluated for violations rather than numeric scores, and each has a priority of Low, Medium, or High. You need the Omnichannel Administrator role, and the page says to set up consumption-based billing and capacity. The page says not to use the feature for employment decisions, and not to infer emotional or psychological states. Build the library, then the plan, then activate it.

chart.title: Two criteria types
chart.note: Different objects. Not a quality target.

lessons.say: An indicator scores. A guardrail flags a required or prohibited behavior. Neither one is an employment decision.
lessons.fault: A prohibited phrase is given a numeric weight because it was entered as an indicator.
lessons.listen: Quality evaluation uses scored indicators and unscored guardrails. Real time and on close are different frequencies. Do not use the score for employment decisions.

lessons.title: Two recording controls
lessons.why: Dynamics can play a recording announcement on the voice channel. Teams compliance recording is a separate policy.
body: The Configure Teams Phone in the voice channel page says that when call recording is enabled, an announcement plays to notify participants. The voice-channel capabilities table also lists transcription and recording, and supervisor record and manage. That is the Dynamics side.

Teams compliance recording is configured with a recording policy and a recording application, on the introduction and setup pages this campus already cites. Enabling the Dynamics announcement does not grant that Teams policy, and granting the Teams policy does not by itself tell you the Dynamics announcement is on. Read both controls. Track 17’s recording room walks the Teams policy objects.

lessons.title: Which control failed
lessons.why: Routing, forecasting, and quality fail in different places. The first control you change should be the one the evidence names.
body: If the work never reaches a queue, read classification and the route-to-queue rules, then the fallback queue. If it reaches the queue and the wrong person gets it, read the assignment method, presence, capacity, and skills. If the queue is staffed for the wrong interval, read the forecast scenario type before you edit the assignment method. If the conversation happened and the score is the dispute, read whether the plan used an indicator or a guardrail, and whether it ran in real time or on close.

Recording is the same habit. Check the Dynamics announcement and the Teams policy separately. None of these controls is an employment action. The assignment, forecast, and quality pages each say not to use them for compensation, rewards, seniority, or similar decisions. The chart is the order you check. It is not a count of incidents.
lessons.say: I name the control that failed before I change a different one.
lessons.fault: A forecast miss is debugged by rewriting the assignment rules.
lessons.listen: Check classification, then assignment, then the forecast type, then the quality plan. Recording stays two controls.
